chunks: And Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Saʿīd al-Azraq, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who killed a believing man, he said:
"It will be said to him: Die whichever death you wish: as a Jew, if you wish, or as a Christian, if you wish, or as a Magian, if you wish."

key_terms.مُؤْمِنًا: a believing person, whose life is inviolable
key_terms.مِيتَةٍ: a mode or manner of death

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the punishment for killing a believer?
ai.summary: This hadith warns with extreme severity against killing a believing person. It portrays the murderer as facing a disgraceful end, expressing the enormity of the sin and its grave consequence in the hereafter.
